papers.title: On the complexity of isomorphism problems for tensors, groups, and polynomials V: over commutative rings
papers.abstract: Tensors over commutative rings naturally appear in number theory, geometry, and group theory. For example, $2\times 2\times 2$ tensors over $\mathbb{Z}$ form the starting point of Bhargava's celebrated works generalising Gauss's composition law (Bhargava, Ann. Math., 2004). Symmetric tensors over $\mathbb{Z}$ are central to the classification of Calabi--Yau threefolds (Yau, Commun. Pure Appl. Math., 1978; Wall, Invent. Math., 1966), geometric objects of significance in string theory. Additionally, tensors over finite commutative rings closely correspond to finite nilpotent groups of class 2 (Baer, Trans. Am. Math. Soc., 1938). In this work, we study isomorphism testing of tensors over commutative rings from a complexity-theoretic viewpoint, and its applications. Some of our main results are: 1. Let $\mathrm{R}$ be a commutative ring. We introduce two complexity classes: $\mathsf{3TI}_\mathrm{R}$ consisting of problems that are polynomial-time reducible to isomorphism problems of tensor products of three modules over $\mathrm{R}$, and $\mathsf{3FTI}_\mathrm{R}$ consisting of problems that are polynomial-time reducible to isomorphism problems of tensor products of three free modules over $\mathrm{R}$. 2. We show that some classical problems considered by Grunewald and Segal (ibid.), and the problem of classifying Calabi--Yau threefolds, are $\mathsf{3FTI}_\mathbb{Z}$-complete. We also show that many natural problems are complete for $\mathsf{3TI}_{\mathbb{Z}/p^e\mathbb{Z}}$. 3. We show that testing isomorphism of tensors in $\mathbb{Z}^2\otimes\mathbb{Z}^2\otimes\mathbb{Z}^2$ is polynomial-time equivalent to the principal ideal problem in algorithmic number theory. 4. We present an $N^{O((\log N)^{8/9})}$-time algorithm for testing isomorphism of finite nilpotent groups of class $2$ and odd order $N$.

papers.title: Deterministic Polynomial-Time Primality Testing with a Single Binomial Congruence
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time primality test whose main verification is the congruence $(1+X)^n=1+X^n$ in $C_n[X]/(X^r-b(Y))$, where $C_n=(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})[Y]/(\Phi_r(Y))$. Two identities in the coefficient ring normalize $b$ and ensure compatibility with the main congruence. A finite-field root count and a lattice bound show that an accepted input is a prime power; elementary preprocessing excludes nontrivial perfect powers. We construct $b$ deterministically using Jacobi sums and the uniform Dedekind-zeta zero-free theorem of Cureton and Thorner, which extends OpenAI's Hecke zero-free theorem. The total bit complexity is $L^{32+o(1)}$, where $L=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$, and verification after constructing $b$ costs $L^{6+o(1)}$. More generally, for a fixed real algebraic $1/2\le\theta<1$, a common zero-free boundary $\Re s>\theta$ for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions gives $L^{\max\{6,(1-\theta)^{-1}\}+o(1)}$. This bound reaches $L^{6+o(1)}$ at $\theta=5/6$, and hence under GRH. We state a fixed-base modification of Agrawal's conjecture for odd integers passing the base-$2$ Fermat test, using the modulus $X^r-2$ with $r$ the least positive integer not dividing $n(n-1)$.

papers.title: Explicit permutations of $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ with uniformly bounded differential uniformity
papers.abstract: Symmetric primitives over Galois rings need nonlinear components whose differentials with respect to ring addition are controlled. Let $R=\mathrm{GR}(4,m)$ and $q=2^m$, so that $(R,+)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ has order $N=q^2$. For every $m\ge1$ we construct an explicit permutation $G_c$ of $R$ all of whose differentials with a nonzero input difference have probability at most $36/N$, whereas every permutation polynomial of $R$ has such a differential of probability at least $2/\sqrt{N}$ (Ronjom--Sandrib). The bound holds for the fixed permutation itself, not on average over keys. Equivalently, $\Delta(G_c)\le36$ against $\Delta\ge2\sqrt{N}$ for permutation polynomials; since every permutation has $\Delta\ge2$, the least differential uniformity of a permutation of $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ lies between $2$ and $36$ for every $m$. In Teichmuller digits $(a,b)\in\mathbb{F}_q^2$ and for $c\in\mathbb{F}_q$ of absolute trace $1$, $G_c(a,b)=(L,(L^2+L+c)a)$ with $L=(a^2+a+c)b$. The map is $F_c\circ J\circ F_c$, where $F_c(a,b)=(a,(a^2+a+c)b)$ is induced by a polynomial over $R$ and $J$ exchanges the digits: a single digit exchange between two polynomial layers yields a bound independent of $m$. The proof reduces the difference equations, in each of three types of directions, to one-variable polynomials whose degrees do not depend on $m$. For general maps $F\circ J\circ F$ with $F(a,b)=(p(a),h(a)+d(a)b)$, where $p,d,h$ have degrees bounded independently of $m$, $p'\ne0$ and $d$ has no zeros, a Jacobian identity in characteristic $2$ bounds the differentials with nonzero low input and output differences independently of $m$; the remaining directions need a separate argument, which we give for an explicit family ($\Delta\le440$, resp. $510$, for odd $m$).

papers.title: Making Every Number from 1 to N Under a Fixed Cycle of $+$, $\times$, $-$, $\div$
papers.abstract: Start with the number $2$. At each move, combine two numbers already made, but the operations must be used in the fixed repeating order $+,\times,-,\div$. We ask for the fewest moves needed to make every integer from $1$ to $N$. Since $2$ is already one of the numbers we want and each move makes at most one new number, at least $N-1$ moves are needed. We show that $N-1$ moves are also enough for every $N\ge 9$. Conventional induction cannot work, because a division that comes right after a completed interval $\{1,\dots,P\}$ produces numbers already made. Instead we extend a completed interval $\{1,\dots,P\}$ to $\{1,\dots,3P\}$ all at once, which counting shows is the smallest multiplicative extension $P\to kP$ that can work, and then adjust the last few moves to reach every other $N$. For $9\le N\le 33$ we give explicit sequences, found by computer search.

papers.title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $\eta_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{\eta_i,\eta_j\in S:\eta_i\neq\eta_j}|\mathcal N(\eta_i-\eta_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.

papers.title: Good rational functions up to degree six
papers.abstract: Locally recoverable codes (LRCs) are fundamental to the architecture of modern distributed storage systems. The Tamo-Barg construction of optimal LRCs was revolutionized by the introduction of good polynomials, which group evaluation points into local recovery sets. However, polynomial constructions are constrained by their inherently large Galois groups, which limit the number of totally split rational places. Recent advances have generalized this paradigm to good rational functions, which leverage the geometry of the projective line to achieve minimal Galois groups and subsequently codes with greater length. In this paper, we complete the classification of good rational functions of degree up to $6$ in characteristic $2$. By embedding the problem into algebraic function field theory, we explicitly determine the minimal arithmetic and geometric Galois groups for these low degrees. Furthermore, we move beyond asymptotic Hasse-Weil estimates by proving that the exact number of totally split places over extension fields obeys a linear recurring sequence (LRS). This gives an efficient method for computing the exact lengths and dimensions of the corresponding optimal LRCs and, in many cases, yields parameters beyond those obtainable from good polynomials.

papers.title: Cyclotomic polynomials with trinomial irreducible factors over finite fields
papers.abstract: We classify the pairs $(q,n)$, where $q$ is a prime power, $n>1$, and $\gcd(n,q)=1$, for which every irreducible factor of $\Phi_n(x)$ over $\F_q$ has exactly three nonzero terms. The positive support exponents of these factors have a common greatest common divisor, which gives a unique reduction by a power substitution. The reduced degree is two in odd characteristic and belongs to $\{2,3,4\}$ in characteristic two; the cubic and quartic cases arise by scalar substitution from the layers of orders $7$ and $15$. This yields necessary and sufficient arithmetic conditions on $(q,n)$ and explicit factorizations. Among the classified families, precisely those arising from quartic bases have a divisor layer containing an irreducible factor with more than three terms.

papers.title: The covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code in nine variables is 242
papers.abstract: We prove that the covering radius of the binary first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9) is exactly 242. Equivalently, the maximum nonlinearity of a Boolean function in nine variables is 242. Our proof combines a one-point rigidity theorem with a spectral and computational exclusion of the two larger candidate nonlinearities. We first show that every nine-variable Boolean function of nonlinearity 243 admits a unique one-point modification that raises its nonlinearity to 244: the point to be changed is the vector sum of its support. This part uses exact Walsh-update identities, integer interpolation, rigidity of a quadratic residue, and a sharp Walsh l1 estimate for cubic Boolean functions. To exclude nonlinearity 244, we use Parseval's identity and congruences of integral Walsh coefficients to force an exceptionally restricted spectrum. An associated cubic residue phase must attain the extremal Walsh l1 bound 10240. We eliminate one equality spectrum by hyperplane slicing; the other forces the original Boolean function from the signs of the cubic phase and yields a double-complement-pairing identity for its cubic top part. The classification of alternating trilinear forms over F2, an exact filter of their representatives, and two exhaustive enumerations of 218 quadratic supplements then rule out every remaining candidate. Together with the known construction attaining nonlinearity 242, these arguments establish the asserted covering radius.

papers.title: Integer points close to a transcendental curve: an algorithmic approach
papers.abstract: In this article, we propose an algorithmic approach to determine the integer points located near a transcendental curve. This approach is closely related to a celebrated work by Bombieri and Pila and to the so-called Coppersmith's method. We establish the underlying theoretical foundations, prove the algorithms, study their complexity and present practical experiments; we also compare our approach with previously existing ones. From a practical point of view, we focus on an instance of our general problem, called the Table Maker's Dilemma, whose solving makes it possible to evaluate a given function with correct rounding. Our experiments show a significant speedup. In particular, our results show that the development of a correctly rounded mathematical library for the binary128 format is now possible at a much smaller cost than with previously existing approaches.

papers.title: On potential density of rational points on hyperkahler varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the rational points on hyperk\"ahler varieties in each of the four known deformation families admitting a rational Lagrangian fibration are potentially dense. Furthermore, we give several applications and construct examples of hyperk\"ahler varieties beyond these families satisfying the potential density property. Our approach is first to prove that rational points on hyperk\"ahler varieties admitting two rational Lagrangian fibrations with distinct associated isotropic rays are potentially dense. We then construct a projective Shafarevich--Tate twist admitting two such fibrations, together with a dominant rational map from the twist to the original variety.

papers.title: Stacked-bases Properties, maximal ideals and polynomial closures of Rings of Integer-Valued Polynomials
papers.abstract: We study the integer-valued polynomial ring with the stacked-bases property, maximal ideals above valuation ideals, and the polynomial closure of matrices with prescribed characteristic polynomials. A content argument gives stacked-bases properties for integer-valued polynomial rings over number-field integer rings. The construction of Hagg and Mortberg provides a Bezout domain without this property. For rank-one valuation domains, maximal ideals are described by evaluations and pseudo-convergent sequences. For matrices, we give congruence-ideal and companion-lattice criteria, together with finite-level tests to characterize the polynomial closures.

papers.title: Topological transcendence degree and the dimension problem for perfectoid spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a perfectoid field of characteristic $p$ with countable value group (for example, $K=\mathbb{C}_{p}^{\flat}$). We study Zariski-closed subsets \begin{equation*}Z\subseteq \mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}\end{equation*}of the $n$-dimensional perfectoid closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}$ over $K$. We use an example of Gleason, and its generalization obtained in the authors' previous work, to show that two natural notions of dimension for such Zariski-closed subsets, the Krull dimension $\dim(Z)$ and Huber's iterated transcendence degree $\mathrm{dim.tr}(Z)$, do not coincide, and that the gap between them can be arbitrarily large.

papers.title: Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of cuspidal coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of local L-parameters. We give a complete classification and relate them to Lusztig's cuspidal local systems (or character sheaves). Under the categorical local Langlands conjecture, these sheaves are expected to correspond to supercuspidal representations supported at basic points. We also construct semiorthogonal decompositions of the category of coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of L-parameters that conjecturally match the semiorthogonal decompositions of sheaves on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ coming from the stratification by the Kottwitz set and Bernstein decomposition of representation categories.

papers.title: A Global Generic Locus for Elementary Abelian p-covers of P^1 with two Ramification Points
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study elementary abelian $p$-covers of $P^1$ totally ramified at exactly two points and unramified elsewhere. Such covers are isomorphic to the rank-$\ell$ Artin--Schreier curves $ X_{f, \ell} : y^{p^\ell} - y = f(x), $ where $f \in \bar{F}_p[x^{\pm 1}]$ has a pole of order $d_1>0$ at $0$ and order $d_2>0$ at $\infty$. After fixing $d_1$ and $d_2$, the cover $X_{f, \ell}$ is generic if its Newton polygon is minimal as $f$ varies over all Laurent polynomials with pole orders $d_1$ and $d_2$. For $p$ sufficiently large relative to $d_1$ and $d_2$, we construct a combinatorial cost polygon $GL(d_1,d_2,p)$ and prove that its attainment is characterized by the nonvanishing of a homogeneous polynomial in the coefficients of $f$. Moreover, we prove that these conditions stabilize: there exists a Zariski-open dense subset $U$ in the coefficient space that is defined over $\Q$ and depends only on $d_1$ and $d_2$, whereby for any $f$ whose coefficients lie in $U(\overline{\Q})$, the reduction is generic at every prime ideal above sufficiently large rational primes, and for every rank $\ell$ permitted by the residue field. This result extends Zhu's result for one ramification point.

papers.title: Calogero-Moser Polynomial Approximations and Dwork Congruences for Complete Flags
papers.abstract: We construct $p$-adic polynomial approximations to the zero-framing cohomological quasimap vertex of cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties from the trigonometric Calogero--Moser system. Negative integer couplings give regular staircase Jack polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. We compare them with complete-flag master polynomials extending the construction of Smirnov--Varchenko. Both families converge coefficientwise to the vertex and satisfy the full commuting equations modulo $p^s$. For $n\geq3$, we prove sharp degree-dependent congruences and compute leading residues at every $p$-power scale. Their discrepancy has coefficient norm $p^{-1}$ and an exact weighted Gauss norm giving uniform decay on smaller closed polydiscs. For the master family, multivariable Dwork congruences reconstruct the vertex by an infinite product. The results hold in every rank for $0<r/d\leq1/2$ and odd prime $p$.

papers.title: Positive integral points on Mordell-Schinzel surfaces
papers.abstract: We apply the theory of generalised cluster algebras to classify the finiteness of positive integral points on the class of log K3 surfaces defined by $xyz = G(x,y)$ where $G$ has positive coefficients. We furthermore establish results on Zariski density, number of orbits and asymptotic growth of such points. These provide a Diophantine realisation of the finite-affine-indefinite trichotomy of rank-two root systems.

papers.title: Isogeny rigidity under algebraic group actions and finite translation orbits
papers.abstract: We study finite orbits generated by fibrewise translations on varieties carrying two abelian fibrations. Under natural dominance and generation hypotheses, non-isotriviality of the first family forces points with finite orbit to lie over proper closed subsets of both bases. This extends results of Corvaja, Tsimerman and Zannier to complex families of arbitrary, possibly different relative dimensions, including torsors. The proof combines relative Manin-Mumford with a general isogeny rigidity theorem for algebraic group actions.

papers.title: Igusa Stacks and the Cohomology of Shimura Varieties
papers.abstract: We construct functorial Igusa stacks for all Hodge-type Shimura varieties, proving a conjecture of Scholze and extending earlier results of the fourth-named author for PEL-type Shimura varieties. Using the Igusa stack, we construct a sheaf on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ that controls the cohomology of the corresponding Shimura variety. We use this sheaf and the spectral action of Fargues-Scholze to prove a compatibility between the cohomology of Shimura varieties of Hodge type and the semisimple local Langlands correspondence of Fargues-Scholze, generalizing the Eichler-Shimura relation of Blasius-Rogawski to arbitrary level at $p$. When the given Shimura variety is proper, we show moreover that the sheaf is perverse, which allows us to prove new torsion vanishing results for the cohomology of Shimura varieties.

papers.title: Minimal $a$-numbers of Artin--Schreier covers of ordinary curves
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $d$ be a positive integer not divisible by $p$. We define a non-empty Zariski open subset $U$ of the space of polynomials of degree $d$, and for $f(x)\in U(k)$, we compute the $a$-number of the curve defined by $y^p-y=f(x)$. This $a$-number realizes a lower bound given by Booher and Cais, so the latter is tight. Our result also implies that the bound of Booher and Cais for minimal $a$-numbers of Artin-Schreier covers of ordinary curves is tight.

papers.title: The Siegel-Weil formula in geometry and arithmetic
papers.abstract: The present paper is an extended version of the lecture notes of a course given by the first author at the summer school on Formulas of Siegel and Weil (Bielefeld, September 2025). We survey three perspectives on the Siegel-Weil formula: classical, geometric, and arithmetic. We first recall the Siegel-Weil formula for elliptic theta series arising from positive definite lattices. We next discuss the higher genus case for lattices of arbitrary signature from an adelic viewpoint. After introducing orthogonal Shimura varieties, we present the geometric Siegel-Weil formula, in which the generating series of volumes of special cycles is shown to be an Eisenstein series. We conclude with the (partly conjectural) arithmetic Siegel-Weil formula, relating degrees of special cycles in arithmetic Chow groups to central derivatives of Eisenstein series.

papers.title: The Dilate Rollercoaster
papers.abstract: Given a finite subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ and a multiset of non-zero integers $\Lambda=\{\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_k\}$, the dilate sum \[\Lambda\cdot A:=\lambda_1\cdot A+\lambda_2\cdot A+\cdots+\lambda_k\cdot A =\{\lambda_1a_1+\cdots+\lambda_ka_k: a_1, \ldots, a_k\in A\}.\] For a non-zero real number $r$, say that $\Lambda_2$ $r$-dominates $\Lambda_1$ if we can partition some of the elements of $\Lambda_2$ into blocks summing to the elements of $r\cdot\Lambda_1$. Then for all finite subsets $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, $\Lambda_2\cdot A$ contains a translate of $r\cdot(\Lambda_1\cdot A)$, and hence $|\Lambda_1\cdot A|\le|\Lambda_2\cdot A|$ for all $A$. In a recent paper, Kravitz (arXiv:2606.27087) proves the converse: if $\Lambda_2$ does not $r$-dominate $\Lambda_1$ for any $r$, then there exists a finite set $A$ satisfying $|\Lambda_1\cdot A|>|\Lambda_2\cdot A|$. For example, $\{2, 3, 5, 7\}$ does not contain two disjoint subsets with a sum ratio of 7, and so there exists a finite $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ for which $|A+7\cdot A|>|2\cdot A+3\cdot A+5\cdot A+7\cdot A|$. We extend Kravitz's method to apply it to multiple inequalities and multiple sets, showing that for multisets $\Lambda_{i,j}$ with $1\le i\le k$ and $1\le j\le\ell$, there exist finite sets $A_1, \ldots, A_\ell\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ such that for all $1\le i<k$ \[|\Lambda_{i,1}\cdot A_1+\cdots+\Lambda_{i,\ell}\cdot A_\ell| >|\Lambda_{i+1,1}\cdot A_1+\cdots+\Lambda_{i+1,\ell}\cdot A_\ell|\] provided there do not exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2\le k$ and a non-zero scalar $r$ such that $\Lambda_{i_2,j}$ $r$-dominates $\Lambda_{i_1,j}$ for all $1\le j\le\ell$. Along the way, we resolve the analogue of Nathanson's Problem 1 for his Theorem 4 (arXiv:1604.08940), as well as the problems in Section 1.4.3 of Kravitz's paper.

papers.title: Identities for generalized Bernoulli numbers from a Lie model of the 2-disk
papers.abstract: We define generalized Bernoulli numbers as appropriate coefficients of the Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff (BCH) product formula, extending the classical sequence of rational numbers to a 2-dimensional setting. We give an identity involving these numbers and the classical Bernoulli numbers which is equivalent to the existence of a particular complete differential graded Lie algebra modelling a cell decomposition of the 2-disk and based on the Lawrence--Sullivan model of the interval. From this identity we derive explicit quadratic relations. The existence of Lie models for the symmetries of the interval and the disk is related to certain properties of the BCH product and to some notable features of the classical Bernoulli numbers: the two choices for $B_1$, the vanishing of $B_n$ for odd $n\geq 3$, and the equality $B_4=B_8$.

papers.title: The Golden Quadruple: Four Reals Whose Differences Form a Geometric Progression, Rigidity of the Golden Ratio, and a Bohr Almost Periodic Cosine Sum
papers.abstract:
Let $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. The four-point set $\{0,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3\}$ is classical: up to a dilation it consists of the two endpoints and the two crossing points on a side of the regular pentagram (Euclid, Elements XIII.8), and, by the identity $\varphi^2=\varphi+1$, its six pairwise differences are $1,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3$, with multiplicities $1,2,2,1$. We write this configuration as the golden quadruple $S=(F, F-a, F-b, F-a-b)$, where $u>0$, $a=\varphi u$, $b=\varphi^2u$ and $F>a+b$, and study its extremal and rigidity properties. We prove that it is maximal and unique: no five distinct real numbers have all their positive differences in $\{u,\varphi u,\varphi^2u,\varphi^3u\}$ (indeed, not even in the whole set $\{u\varphi^n:n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$), and every four-element set with this property is a translate of $S$. We prove that the golden ratio is forced: $\varphi$ is the only ratio $x>1$ for which some four-point set of reals has the four-term progression $\{c,cx,cx^2,cx^3\}$ as its set of distinct differences. For the analogous quadruple with base $x>1$, $x
eq\varphi$, the failure is measured by two closure residues, $(x^2-x-1)u$ and $x(x^2-x-1)u$, which along Fibonacci quotients equal $\pm u/F_n^2$ and $\pm F_{n+1}u/F_n^3$. Finally, the cosine sum $C_S(t)=\sum\cos(2\pi d t)$ over the six differences equals $8\cos^2(\pi a t)\cos^2(\pi b t)-2$; it is not periodic, but it is almost periodic in the sense of Bohr, with explicit almost periods $F_n/u$. For an arbitrary scale $K>0$ the golden ladder $
u_n=K\varphi^{-n}$ realises the construction with $u=
u_{203}$, so that the differences are $
u_{200},\dots,
u_{203}$; we evaluate it for $K=\sqrt{c^5/(Gh)}$. We state explicitly what is classical and what is new, in relation to difference sets, Golomb rulers, Sidon sets, Fibonacci numbers, quasicrystals and almost periodic functions.

papers.title: Halving Partitions and Hyperbinary Expansions
papers.abstract: Starting from a positive integer, repeatedly halve the current value, rounding up or down. Which resulting sequences have terms that add to the starting integer? A simple balance identity turns the rounding choices into hyperbinary expansions, in which each power of two occurs at most twice. This correspondence gives exact counts by length and an injection into the expansions counted by Stern's diatomic sequence. We characterize equality in the resulting bound by the binary digits of the odd part of the integer. We also determine the unique longest partition and give a short recursive counting algorithm. When the required total is allowed to vary, the chain counts eventually equal Stern's number, and we determine the exact threshold. A direct proof shows that the counts of hyperbinary expansions in the three length classes modulo three differ by at most one. For sufficiently long halving partitions, the counts by length first weakly increase and then weakly decrease, although the full sequence need not do so.

papers.title: Contact multiplicity and a sharp six-map bound for collinear self-similar dendrites
papers.abstract: Let $K\subset\mathbb{C}$ be the attractor of $n\ge2$ similarities $z\mapsto\lambda z+b_k$, $0<|\lambda|<1$, whose fixed points are evenly spaced on a line, and suppose that $K$ does not lie in a line. We prove that $K$ can be a dendrite only if $n\le6$, and that such dendrites exist for every $2\le n\le6$; no separation or finite-intersection hypothesis is imposed. Hence, for $n\ge7$, every connected $K$ of this kind has interior points or separates the plane. Neighboring pieces of $K$ meet in similar copies of a single contact set. In a dendrite exactly one first-level piece meets this set, whereas for $n\ge7$ at least $n-\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil\ge2$ do, a bound attained by explicit quadratic parameters. The proof combines a planar translation obstruction for replicated contact arcs with an estimate based on Jensen's formula. After normalizing to $z\mapsto t+z/c$, $t\in\{-n+1,-n+3,\ldots,n-1\}$, the connectedness locus is the closure, outside the unit disk, of the roots of monic integer polynomials of height at most $n-1$. The same estimate shows that, for $n\ge7$, every such polynomial with a non-real root $c$ satisfying $|c|^2\ge\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil+1$ has subleading coefficient of absolute value at most $\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$, and that this bound is sharp. Accordingly, for $n\ge7$, at every non-real boundary point $c$ of the locus with $|c|>1$, each expansion $c=\sum_{j\ge0}d_jc^{-j}$ with integer digits $|d_j|\le n-1$ has $|d_0|\le\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$.

papers.title: Counterexamples to uniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform under quadratic decay
papers.abstract: We show nonuniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform on $\mathbb Z^2$ under quadratic decay. We construct an explicit nonzero function in $\ell^1(\mathbb Z^2)$ with pointwise decay $O(|z|^{-2})$ whose sums over integer lines vanish. We also obtain an infinite-dimensional null space with the same decay assumption. Furthermore, we show a result which indicates that the decay rate $|z|^{-2}$ may be sharp and faster decay may imply uniqueness.

papers.title: An Odd-Arch Family of Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursions: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws
papers.abstract: For every integer $p\ge2$, we construct a globally well-defined positive odd sequence $Q_p$ satisfying, after an explicit finite initial block, $Q_p(n)=Q_p(n-Q_p(n-1))+Q_p(n-Q_p(n-2))-(-1)^n$. Its binary block words admit the exact factorization $U_{p,k}=(A_k\overline{A}_{k+1})^{p-1}A_{k+2}$, producing exactly $2p-1$ alternating signed arches per natural block. The elementary word heights converge uniformly to the Gaussian isoperimetric profile $\varphi\circ\Phi^{-1}$. For each fixed $p$, this yields an explicit dyadic limiting profile with $2p-1$ sign transitions and a sharp relative-error constant $\Lambda_p=b_p/2$, where $b_p$ is determined by $b_p((3p-1)/2+\Phi(-b_p))=\varphi(b_p)$. We determine all zeros and parity crossings in sufficiently large dyadic blocks. For $p\ge3$, there are exactly $2p-1$ transverse even-index zeros, whereas the three-arch case $p=2$ exhibits an alternating four/six-zero pattern. An ordered frequency factorization gives exact dyadic histograms, moments, total-variation distances, and extremal multiplicities. The limiting frequency generating function $z^3/(2-z)$ is universal, although the highest finite multiplicities depend on $p$. Finally, the summatory function has main terms $N^2/4+(N/2)\log_2N$, an explicit parameter-dependent log-periodic term of order $N$, and remainder $O_p(N/\sqrt{\log N})$.

papers.title: Infinite Generalized Sidon Sets with a Negative Answer to a Problem of Szemer\'edi
papers.abstract: We construct infinite $B_h$ sets that repeatedly attain the density scale of finite $B_h$ sets. For every integer $h\geq2$ and every finite $B_h$ set $F$ of positive integers, we obtain an infinite $B_h$ set $A\supseteq F$ such that $$ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=\frac1h, \qquad \liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=0. $$ The key is to preserve density while preventing additive relations between successive blocks. A positional encoding of the finite-field moment curve has $q$ elements in an interval of length $O_h(q^h)$, while, for each $1\leq r<h$, sums arising from distinct $r$-element multisets are separated by more than $q$. This separation allows whole blocks to be appended to a prescribed finite set without a further dilation. In particular, our result gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Szemer\'edi \cite{szemeredi}.

papers.title: The signed error-sum function of tent-map expansions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the signed error-sum function of tent map base series introduced by Dai and Tang in 2011. We show that the function is discontinuous at every dyadic rational in the open unit interval, although it was asserted to be continuous. We determine its values at these points and analyze its range, differentiability, and variation. We also obtain sharp covering estimates for its graph and calculate the Hausdorff, box-counting, and covering dimensions of the graph, which are $1$, $1$, and $0$, respectively. Moreover, we show that the signed error sum agrees with L\'evy's function away from dyadic rationals and that the unsigned error sum is the Takagi function.

papers.title: On a hybrid trilinear Hilbert transform
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the boundedness properties of a \emph{hybrid} trilinear Hilbert transform characterized by a \emph{dual regime} which simultaneously exhibits 1) \emph{resonant} (zero curvature) features, \emph{i.e.}, modulation invariance properties, and 2) \emph{non-resonant} (non-zero curvature) features. Specifically, given $a\in(0,\infty)\setminus \{1,2\}$ and $\vec{\lambda}:=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4)\in (\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\})^4$ with $\lambda_1\neq \lambda_2$ and $\lambda_3\neq \lambda_4$, we provide wide-range $L^p$ bounds for the trilinear operator $$ HTHT^a_{\vec{\lambda}} (f_1,f_2,f_3)(x):= p.v. \int_{\mathbb R} f_1(x-\lambda_1 t)\,f_2(x-\lambda_2 t-\lambda_3 t^a)\,f_3(x-\lambda_4 t^a)\,\frac{dt}{t},\quad x \in \mathbb{R}\,.$$ By combining variable multiresolution, multiscale wave-packet analysis, and Rank II LGC method, our present work establishes a common framework where the diverse methodologies of all of the following naturally converge: i) the maximal truncated bilinear Hilbert transform, ii) the Biest operator, iii) the hybrid bilinear Hilbert-Carleson operator, and iv) the non-resonant (curved) trilinear Hilbert transform. Ultimately, this work reveals that the hybrid trilinear transform sits on a critical intermediate scale between the purely non-resonant case and the purely resonant regime -- the latter remaining a challenging, major (open) problem in harmonic analysis.
